title: LoRA / QLoRA Fine-Tuning
summary: Adapt a base model through low-rank trainable updates, optionally over a quantized frozen base, with explicit compatibility and evaluation controls.
overview: LoRA trains low-rank update matrices for selected model layers while keeping the base weights frozen. This can reduce trainable parameter and optimizer-state requirements compared with full fine-tuning. QLoRA combines low-rank adaptation with a quantized frozen base to reduce training memory further; it does not mean that all model parameters are trained in low-bit form.

Adapters are dependent artifacts. Their meaning depends on the base model revision, target modules, tokenizer, and training configuration. Fine-tuning changes behavior and task fit; it is usually a poor substitute for retrieval when the main requirement is frequently updated factual knowledge. Adapter training still requires governed data and careful held-out evaluation.

production.poc: A prototype compares prompting and retrieval baselines with a small adapter trained on clean task examples.
production.production: Production versions data, base weights, adapter settings, and evaluation results, then validates the exact serving configuration.
production.scale: Enterprise scale handles many adapters, tenant isolation, loading latency, reproducible training, and rollback of both behavior and deployment artifacts.

components.name: Training dataset
components.role: Contains reviewed task demonstrations with rights, provenance, and leakage controls.

components.name: Frozen base model
components.role: Provides the pretrained representation under a pinned revision.

components.name: Low-rank adapter trainer
components.role: Optimizes selected update matrices with recorded rank and target modules.

components.name: Evaluation suite
components.role: Measures task quality, safety behavior, and regressions beyond training examples.

components.name: Adapter registry and server
components.role: Stores compatible artifacts and loads or merges them according to supported runtime behavior.

flow.title: Confirm adaptation need
flow.description: Show that prompting, retrieval, or schema controls do not adequately solve the behavior gap.

flow.title: Prepare governed examples
flow.description: Clean demonstrations and split evaluation by source or time to avoid leakage.

flow.title: Configure the adapter
flow.description: Choose target modules, rank, precision, and training settings within the hardware budget.

flow.title: Train reproducibly
flow.description: Record base revision, tokenizer, data lineage, and checkpoints.

flow.title: Evaluate the served artifact
flow.description: Test the adapter with the exact quantization and runtime intended for deployment.

flow.title: Promote gradually
flow.description: Canary the model-adapter pair and retain the previous approved pair for rollback.

useCase.title: Adapting a correspondence extraction style
useCase.situation: A business-services team needs consistent extraction of a specialized correspondence schema.
useCase.problem: Prompt examples improve results but remain inconsistent on recurring domain phrasing.
useCase.requirement: Learn the extraction behavior while keeping changing reference facts in retrieval.
useCase.architecture: A LoRA adapter trains on reviewed examples and is evaluated against unseen source organizations.
runtime: The training pipeline records base and dataset revisions.
The served adapter is tested for exact schema validity and field accuracy before a small rollout.
useCase.failure: If the adapter improves common fields but harms rare exception fields, promotion stops until the data or training configuration is corrected.
useCase.impact: Measure field-level accuracy, invalid-output rate, and total training plus serving cost; fewer trainable parameters do not remove evaluation obligations.

tradeoffs.cost: May have limited capacity for some behavior changes.

tradeoffs.benefit: Support specialized behaviors on one base.
tradeoffs.cost: Complicate routing, isolation, and artifact management.

failures.detection: Quality degrades or tensor compatibility checks fail.
failures.recovery: Enforce exact base and tokenizer lineage before loading.
Split by source lineage and audit near duplicates.

mistakes.mistake: Using fine-tuning to refresh volatile facts

mistakes.fix: Measure held-out task and regression performance.
Validate base, target modules, precision, and runtime compatibility.

whenToUse: Use for stable task behavior and specialized output patterns.
Use when clean demonstrations are available.
Use when full fine-tuning exceeds the justified resource budget.
whenNotToUse: Avoid adaptation for facts that change frequently.
Do not train on unreviewed sensitive feedback automatically.
Avoid deployment without exact serving-bundle evaluation.
